newsitem.title: FRANCE: Serge Dassault fined for illegal hunting.
newsitem.headline: Serge Dassault fined for illegal hunting.

text.p: A French court on Monday fined Serge Dassault, chairman of jetfighter maker Dassault Aviation, for illegally shooting deer from a turret mounted on the roof of a four-wheel drive vehicle.

The court in Rambouillet west of Paris fined Dassault 10,000 francs ($1,740), banned him from hunting for a year and confiscated his specially-converted vehicle. It also fined his driver, Alain Weislinger, 3,000 francs ($520).
Dassault, 71, was formally fined for "hunting with banned means" on his private estate.

At a court hearing in March, he had admitted via a spokesman that he had hunted for years with a high-calibre rifle while standing in his vehicle in a padded turret mounted in the roof while his driver chased game.
Game wardens inspected the private estate because of the unexpectedly large number of deer Dassault was bagging.

The court said Dassault, whose company makes the Mirage and Rafale combat jets, and Weislinger will also have to pay a combined 10,000 francs ($1,740) to associations who had been civil parties to the court action.
Dassault, a member of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist party, is the mayor of the town of Corbeil-Essonne south of Paris.
